candidates.phrase: He is infinite in power, wisdom, justice, goodness and love
candidates.rationale: The Confession directly predicates infinite goodness of God himself with an unambiguous pronoun, squarely meeting the floor of shared divine goodness.
candidates.chunk_text: We believe in the one true, holy and living God, Eternal Spirit, who is Creator, Sovereign and Preserver of all things visible and invisible. He is infinite in power, wisdom, justice, goodness and love, and rules with gracious regard for the well-being and salvation of men, to the glory of his name. We believe the one God reveals himself as the Trinity: Father, Son and Holy Spirit, distinct but inseparable, eternally one in essence and power.

candidates.locator: Article I — Of Faith in the Holy Trinity
candidates.phrase: living and true God, everlasting, without body or parts, of infinite power, wisdom, and goodness
candidates.rationale: The Article predicates infinite goodness of the one living and true God, asserting the floor's shared divine goodness of the required subject.
candidates.chunk_text: There is but one living and true God, everlasting, without body or parts, of infinite power, wisdom, and goodness; the maker and preserver of all things, both visible and invisible. And in unity of this Godhead there are three persons, of one substance, power, and eternity—the Father, the Son, and the Holy Ghost.

candidates.chunk_text: We believe in the one living and true God, both holy and loving, eternal, unlimited in power, wisdom and goodness, the Creator and Preserver of all things.
